citations.title: About | Trusaic
excerpts: Robert Sheen is the Founder and CEO of Trusaic. He leads the company’s mission to help global enterprises make precise, compliant pay decisions at scale — turning every pay decision into measurable progress.

Robert began his career as a tax attorney at KPMG and BDO before founding First Capitol Consulting, Inc. in 1999. He also founded and chartered US Metro Bank, an early adopter of remote check capture technology that has grown to more than $1.5 billion in assets.

What began as a regulatory technology company focused on tax savings, compliance, and business intelligence evolved into Trusaic. Under Robert’s leadership, Trusaic has pioneered a category-defining approach that combines data, regulatory expertise, and purpose-built software to solve complex workforce challenges. Today, Trusaic’s Pay Equity Software Suite helps organizations build unbiased, legally-defensible pay systems across global workforces.

Robert continues to shape the future of pay equity and transparency by helping organizations navigate complexity and strengthen accountability in their pay practices. His work is grounded in a clear belief: that fair pay is a fundamental right, and that with the right systems in place, every pay decision can move organizations closer to achieving it.

Trusaic also delivers industry-leading ACA compliance solutions, combining data integration, regulatory expertise, and fully managed services to help organizations reduce risk, streamline reporting, and stay audit-ready year-round.

excerpts: Trusaic Introduces Enhanced EU Pay Transparency Directive Monitor with Interactive Map as Member States Diverge Ahead of June Transposition Deadline
# Trusaic Introduces Enhanced EU Pay Transparency Directive Monitor with Interactive Map as Member States Diverge Ahead of June Transposition Deadline
_**Only 2 of 27 member states are on track to meet the deadline.**_
_**Enhanced monitoring capabilities help multinational employers track evolving national requirements.**_

_Los Angeles, CA – May 20, 2026_ – Global pay equity and transparency technology company Trusaic has enhanced its [EU Pay Transparency Directive Transposition Monitor](https://trusaic.com/resources/resources-eu-pay-transparency-directive-member-state-transposition-monitor/?utm_campaign=Brand%20Persona&utm_content=377602716&utm_medium=social&utm_source=linkedin&hss_channel=lcp-40807422) with a real-time interactive map to help employers track evolving national implementation measures ahead of the Directive’s 7 June, 2026 deadline. To date, several member states have published draft legislation, while others remain at earlier stages of transposition. Though the transposition deadline is rapidly approaching, only 2 of 27 member states are currently on track to meet it. This creates ambiguity for employers having to navigate inconsistent implementation that will extend past the EU Commission’s intended June deadline.

The EU Pay Transparency Directive (EUPTD) establishes a common framework intended to strengthen pay equity and transparency across the European Union. However, national transposition activity is advancing at differing speeds across member states, with variations emerging in legislative scope, reporting obligations and enforcement approaches. For employers operating across multiple jurisdictions, this evolving regulatory landscape is increasing compliance complexity and creating additional legal, operational and governance considerations.

“As of now, eight member states have confirmed delays, with Romania potentially joining, and 14 have no draft legislation at all,” says Robert Sheen, CEO, Trusaic. “The challenge for multinational employers is managing the growing divergence in how member states are implementing it. Organizations need continuous visibility into national developments as compliance expectations evolve across Europe.”

Although many organizations monitor legislative developments, the pace and variability of national transposition activity makes static tracking tools increasingly insufficient. Trusaic’s enhanced Transposition Monitor tracks country-by-country legislative developments, helping legal, HR and compliance teams assess readiness as the Directive approaches enforcement.
* Interactive map highlighting member state status with easy, direct navigation to each state
* Ongoing tracking of member state transposition activity
* Jurisdiction-specific implementation updates including projected effective dates

basis.reasoning: Trusaic’s press announcement is dated May 20, 2026 and says it enhanced the EU Pay Transparency Directive Monitor with a real-time interactive map, a major feature release within the six-month window.
